maya: Quick heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion for a community gpt-small-spm produced resegmentation where <|pad|> ended up inside the middle of token sequences, causing encoder alignment shift in our eval run. Repro steps below.

liam: Can you paste the exact conversion command and the tokenizer files you used?

maya: Command I ran: `python hf_to_redwood.py --model_dir /mnt/models/gpt-small-spm --out /tmp/conv --prefer-bpe=false`
config.json had model_max_length: 2048. There is a model.spm in the repo but no merges.txt.

sasha: If prefer-bpe=false we keep spm pieces, but our Redwood runtime tooling expects bpe-compatible merges for some chat-template heuristics. What did the eval regressions look like?

maya: On quantized int8 runs we see token shifts in 4/9 prompts. Greedy outputs drop function-call markers because the function name token was split unexpectedly. Eg expected `\u003c|fn_call_start|\u003emy_fn\u003c|fn_call_end|\u003e` but got `\u003c|fn_call_start|\u003e my_ f n\u003c|fn_call_end|\u003e` (spaces added from resegmentation).

anita: Do you have a `special_tokens_map.json`? We previously hit a bug where sentinel tokens were mapped to piece strings and then de-duplicated, which changed indices.

maya: special_tokens_map.json existed but mapped to literal piece strings, not final numeric ids. The conversion script generated merges where indices started at 0 instead of offsetting by vocab_size — looks like an off-by-one in the merge writer.

dev-bot: deploy:tokenizer-conv 1991234600 started conversion pipeline for gpt-small-spm

liam: Quick checks: dump the spm proto order. Example: `python -c "import sentencepiece as spm; sp=spm.SentencePieceProcessor(); sp.Load('model.spm'); print([sp.IdToPiece(i) for i in range(20)])"` Also compare `vocab_size` from config vs `model_proto.pieces_size()`.

maya: I dumped pieces — the special token `\u003c|pad|\u003e` is at index 3 in the spm proto, but after conversion the same string became id 1027. So duplicates were removed and ordering changed.

sasha: Hypothesis: the merge builder does `sorted(set(pieces))` somewhere which reorders pieces alphabetically. That will break any code relying on stable piece order. Workaround: preserve the original piece order by iterating `model_proto.pieces` and writing merges in that order.

anita: For an immediate mitigation, try rebuilding the tokenizer with a flag to preserve order: `python rebuild_tokenizer.py --spm model.spm --bpe-out tokenizer.json --preserve-order` then re-run your eval.

maya: Ran rebuild — regressions dropped from 4/9 to 1/9. The remaining failure is on an emoji+ZWJ prompt. Suspect unicode normalization differences (NFKC vs NFC) between SentencePiece and our pretokenizer.

liam: Add an explicit normalizer in conversion config: "normalizer": "nfkc" and pass `--normalize=true` to the conversion script. Also add a unit test that tokenizes a set of canonical inputs and compares piece ids between HF and Redwood converter.

maya: Will patch the conversion script, add tests that assert piece_id(order) equality and a small fuzz suite for emoji/ZWJ cases. Filing a short RFC after I get a clean repro. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
